_disambiguation_notes: Axis 1 - 'remember'-led four-way split (create_list_v1 / save_preference_v1 / remember_topic_v1 / log_item_location_v1):
log_item_location_v1: locative frame 'where I put/left/placed X' -> location, strongest syntactic marker.
save_preference_v1: preference marker (favourite/preferred/favorite) + category + multiple items.
create_list_v1: collection under a name - list-word (list/checklist) and/or multiple items, imperative creation verb, NO preference marker, NO single copula binding.
remember_topic_v1: single topic->value binding, usually an is/are copula - 'my X is Y'. One fact, one value.
Axis 2 - create_list_v1 vs recall_stored_info_v1 (the original misroute axis):
create_list_v1: imperative + declares NEW items ('make/create/start a ... list <items>').
recall_stored_info_v1: interrogative + NO new items ('what's on my ... list', 'show my ...'). Bare names ('my swimming list') are caught upstream by _preempt_known_data_recall before the router runs.

Curation warning: 'remember my' is a shared prefix across three intents above, so their embedding centroids are inherently close and the margin threshold is thin there. Keep distinctive frames ('make a checklist...', 'start a packing list...') dominant for create_list_v1 - do not let 'remember my' become its lead form.
Keys prefixed with '_' are metadata, not intents - semantic_router.py must skip them when building the vector bank.
